chunks: 1481 - And Muḥammad ibn al-Fuḍayl narrated from Abū al-Ṣabbāḥ al-Kinānī, who said:

I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the takbīr in the two Eids, and he said: “There are twelve takbīrs: seven in the first and five in the second. When you stand in the salat (prayer), say one takbīr and say: I bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone, having no partner, and I bear witness that Muḥammad is His servant and His Messenger. O Allah, You are worthy of majesty and greatness, and worthy of generosity, omnipotence, power, authority, and might. I ask You on this day which You have made an Eid for the Muslims, and a ذخْر and increase for Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله, to send blessings upon Muḥammad and the family of Muḥammad, and to bless Your near angels and Your sent prophets, and to forgive us and all the believing men and believing women, and the Muslim men and Muslim women, the living among them and the dead. O Allah, I ask You for the best of what Your righteous servants have asked You, and I seek refuge in You from the evil of what Your sincere servants have sought refuge from.”

Allah is the Greatest, the first of everything and its last, the originator of everything and its ultimate end, the knower of everything and its return, and the destination of everything is to Him and its return is to Him, and the arranger of affairs, and the raiser of...

the acceptor of deeds, the initiator of hidden things, and the manifester of secrets. Allah is the Greatest, tremendous in dominion, intense in might, living and not dying, everlasting and not passing away.
“When He decrees a matter, He only says to it: Be, and it is.”

Allah is the Greatest. Voices are humbled to You, faces submit to You, eyes are bewildered before You, and tongues fall short of Your greatness. All forelocks are in Your hand, and the measures of all affairs are to You; none decides in them other than You, and nothing of them is completed without You. Allah is the Greatest. Your protection encompasses everything, Your might overpowers everything, Your command penetrates everything, everything stands through You, everything humbles itself before Your greatness, everything is abased before Your might, everything submits to Your power, and everything yields to Your dominion. Allah is the Greatest.

And you recite al-Ḥamd and “Sabbihi sma Rabbika al-Aʿlā,” then pronounce the seventh takbīr, bow, and prostrate. Then you stand, recite al-Ḥamd and “al-Shamsi wa Ḍuḥāhā,” and say: Allah is the Greatest, I bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone, having no partner, and I bear witness that Muḥammad is His servant and Messenger. O Allah, You are worthy of majesty and greatness. You complete all of it just as you said it at the first takbīr. This statement is to be said in every takbīr until five takbīrs are completed.”

key_terms.التَّكْبِيرِ: the pronouncement of 'Allāhu Akbar' in the Eid prayer
key_terms.الْحَمْدَ: Sūrat al-Ḥamd, the Opening chapter recited in salat
key_terms.الْعِيدَيْنِ: the two Eid festivals, Eid al-Fiṭr and Eid al-Aḍḥā
key_terms.الْمُخْلَصُونَ: the purified or sincere servants devoted to Allah
key_terms.تَكْبِيرَةً: a single takbīr utterance within the prayer
key_terms.مُدَبِّرُ الْأُمُورِ: the One who administers and arranges all affairs

ai.seo_question: How are the takbīrs and supplications performed in the Eid prayer according to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the form of the takbīrs in the Eid salat (prayer), specifying their number in each rakʿah and the supplication to be recited with them. It combines practical prayer rulings with a profound du'a praising Allah’s majesty, power, knowledge, and absolute authority.
